display.purpose: The name on the checklist card and page H1s. Uppercase, hard-broken into two lines, tracking -0.03em.

row-label.purpose: The .chk__label half of the atomic row: mono caps at 0.09em, ink-muted.

shadows.name: sheet-lift

shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system. Lifts a .sheet card a millimetre off the card stock. Never grows on hover; no second shadow may be authored.

motion.name: check-draw
motion.purpose: The signature moment: the check stroke drawing itself via stroke-dasharray 24. Belongs to <Check> and nothing else.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Entrance for non-critical content — 6px rise plus fade. Never used in a first viewport; the hero must be legible at first paint.

motion.name: standby
motion.purpose: Opacity pulse 1 → 0.35 on the active status dot. The only looping animation; must stay attached to a live state.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default hover/focus transition. Colour only — nothing transitions transform, size or shadow.

motion.name: tab-wipe
motion.purpose: The 3px amber underline wiping in from the left on a tab that is hovered, focused, or aria-current.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Neutralises every animation and settles the check to its drawn state. Smooth scrolling is disabled with it.

narrative.overview:
This site is a laminated checklist card and a page torn from a Quick Reference Handbook. Not a metaphor applied as decoration — the structure is the checklist. Every claim on the page is a challenge with a response beside it, joined by leader dots: LOCATION ·········· Boston, Massachusetts. That row is the atom of the entire system. Sections, cards, notices and even the mobile menu are built out of it. The result reads as a procedure that was run, not a pitch that was written.

The material is near-white card stock with a barely-there fibre tooth — a 4px repeating hairline at 1.6% ink, drawn in body::before, not an image. Against it sit brighter sheets, separated by rules rather than shadows. Structure comes from a placard charcoal that owns full-width bands — the fixed tab strip at the top, the Contact section, the footer revision block — and never appears as a tint or a soft background elsewhere. Type is B612 and B612 Mono, the family Airbus and ENAC commissioned for cockpit displays: it is legible under stress, and that is why it is here.

Colour is the strictest rule in the system. It carries state and nothing else. Black is normal, caution amber is in progress, verified green is complete, warning red is failure. There is no brand accent, no gradient, no hue chosen because it looked good. If a colour on a mounted surface cannot be traced to a state a visitor can verify, it is a defect. This world explicitly refuses the centred-hero-over-card-grid portfolio, the soft rounded card, the glass panel, and the decorative accent colour.
keyCharacteristics: Challenge–response leader-dot rows as the universal information unit
Square corners everywhere; the radius scale is effectively zero
Heavy 3px section rules and 1px sub-rules doing the work shadows usually do
Charcoal bands running full bleed; sheets never tinted
Mono placards in caps for every label, index, tab and key
Tabular numerals wherever numbers can be compared
Colour reserved for state: amber / green / red only
One authored motion moment — the check being drawn

rules.name: The State-Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Colour on a mounted surface must name a state a visitor could verify: amber = in progress, green = complete, red = failed. There is no fourth meaning and no brand accent. A hue chosen because a section "needed some colour" is a defect, not a variant.

rules.name: The Band Rule
rules.body: When colour appears, it owns a full band, a 3px marker, a gauge fill, or a 6px dot. It never appears as a wash behind body text and never as a fat coloured border on a card. .notice puts the colour in .notice__band and leaves the body on sheet white for exactly this reason.

rules.name: The Faint Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing lighter than --color-ink-faint may hold text on a light ground, and nothing lighter than --color-panel-muted may hold text on charcoal. There is no "subtle" tier below these — quiet text is ink-faint at full strength, not ink-muted at reduced opacity.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: B612 for prose and headings, B612 Mono for every label, index, tab, button and number. There is no third face, no serif (--font-serif is aliased to B612 and is a shim, not an option), and no system display stack.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number a reader might compare against another number gets .nums. A percentage beside a gauge, an hour count, a date, a 3/6 — all tabular. A number inside a sentence does not need it.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose holds max-w-[62ch] even when the grid column is wider. Pull quotes and lede headlines tighten further — 46ch for a blockquote, 34ch for a callout or card title, 28ch for a standalone page headline.

rules.name: The Challenge–Response Rule
rules.body: Any fact with a name and a value is a .chk row: chk__label + chk__lead (aria-hidden) + chk__value. Do not build a two-column definition list, a bordered key/value table, or a badge pair instead. The row wraps rather than clips — the value may take its own line in a narrow card.

rules.name: The Full-Bleed Band Rule
rules.body: The charcoal panel always spans the full viewport width with its content constrained by the same container. A charcoal card floating inside a light section is not part of this world.

rules.name: The Drawn-Depth Rule
rules.body: Depth is a rule you can point at. If a surface needs to feel separate, give it a border and a heavier rule above it — not a larger shadow. Hover never grows a shadow and never lifts a card.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: .sheet owns the only box-shadow in the system. A new component that wants elevation uses .sheet; it does not author a second shadow value.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: No rounded corners. Not on cards, not on buttons, not on inputs, not on status dots. A pill or a rounded-lg in this world reads as a component imported from a different site.

rules.name: The Placard Key Rule
rules.body: Buttons are square keys. Never a pill, never a shadow that grows on hover, never a gradient, and never smaller than the body text around them — the page's conversion actions must not be its smallest lettering.

dos: Do build every name/value pair as a .chk row via <Row>. It is the atom of this system and the reason the page reads as a procedure.
Do open a new section with <SectionHead index="0N" …> and take the next sequential index.
Do keep colour tied to state — amber in progress, green complete, red failed — and let everything else be ink on card stock.
Do put a state colour in a band, a dot, a 3px marker or a gauge fill, and leave the body text on sheet white or charcoal.
Do use .placard for every small label and .nums for every comparable figure.
Do cap prose at max-w-[62ch] regardless of how wide the grid column is.
Do separate list entries with border-t border-rule and first:border-t-0 rather than with margin alone.
Do wrap any charcoal surface in .on-panel so keyboard focus switches to the amber ring, and pair --color-panel-ink / --color-panel-muted for text on it.
Do draw icons as SVG paths with stroke-linecap="square", matching the check and arrow already in Checklist.jsx.
Do give every interactive target at least 44px (min-h-11 / min-w-11).
donts: Don't round a corner. No rounded-* on cards, buttons, inputs, dots or bars; buttons are square placard keys, never pills.
Don't spend colour decoratively. An amber heading, a green divider, or a tinted card that doesn't report a state is a defect.
Don't put --color-caution text on a light ground — use --color-caution-ink. Amber-on-white does not clear 4.5:1.
Don't hold text in anything lighter than --color-ink-faint (or --color-panel-muted on charcoal), and don't reach for opacity to make text quieter.
Don't author a second box-shadow. .sheet owns the only one, and hover never grows it.
Don't use the charcoal panel as a card tint or a hover fill — it owns full-width bands only.
Don't introduce a third typeface, a serif, or a system display stack. B612 and B612 Mono are the whole vocabulary.
Don't animate for delight. The build has one authored moment; anything beyond it needs a reason a checklist would accept.
Don't use a Unicode character as an icon, or a glyph icon font. Draw the path.
Don't reuse the legacy tokens or classes listed under Compatibility Shim — they are scaffolding for unmounted files, not part of this language.
